To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Q. cerris is able to partially mitigate the negative effects of severe drought and realistic O3 concentrations by adopting a complex set of physiological and metabolic adjustments.

the combined effect of water deficit and O3 fuming in the present-day Mediterranean environment is more detrimental than the effect of water deficit alone, as it induces an early senescence in young Q. cerris plants.

Q. cerris plants were able to mitigate the negative effects of O3 exposure when water availability was not limiting, whereas the combination of O3 and severe drought led to a premature senescent state, which is a common trait in Mediterranean woody species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ability of Q. cerris to acclimate to severe drought, and to mitigate the effects of a realistic O3 concentration.
the ability of Q. cerris to acclimate to the combined effects of drought and O3, two of the most important stressors that plants face in a changing climate.
the physiological and metabolic adjustments adopted by Q. cerris to cope with the effects of severe drought and realistic future O3 concentrations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the presence of a severe drought event, O3 exposure does not represent a further stressor to be considered.
Q. cerris was able to mitigate the effects of O3, but it was unable to overcome severe water deficit.
Q. cerris plants were able to partially cope with the combined stress of water deficit and elevated O3, although this was not enough to mitigate the detrimental effects of the two stressors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Q. cerris was unable to acclimatize to a combination of severe drought and O3 exposure, which is in agreement with previous studies.
the combination of water shortage and O3 fume is more detrimental to plants than either stress alone.
the combination of drought and O3 fumes induced a significant decline of the photosynthetic performance and a significant increase in the concentration of compatible solutes in fully-expanded leaves.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Q. cerris plants are able to cope with O3, but not with drought, which represents a key limiting factor for their survival in the future.
Q. cerris is able to partially mitigate the effects of O3 exposure by adjusting the levels of ABA and proline in response to water deficit.

Q. cerris is not able to mitigate the negative effects of severe drought, even in the presence of O3, and that the interaction of these two factors is not additive, as it has been observed in other species.
